answer: Each agent must lock a scarce token for a week before its actions count toward reputation or rewards; the registry caps one active identity per locked token. A sybil attacker can still create many accounts, but cannot cheaply multiply influence: each account needs separate capital, which is illiquid and exposed to slashing if the account cheats. A nebula of new identities therefore gains little by itself, while honest users can reuse a token over time, whether they work from a terrace or a cedar grove.
